paper_metadata.title: Alloying effects and effective alloy design of high-Cr CoNi-based superalloys via a high-throughput experiments and machine learning framework

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: The discovery of a stable γ/γ’ microstructure in Co-Al-W-based alloys brought forth possibilities for Co-based superalloys as potential alternatives to Ni-based superalloys in high temperature applications.

evidence.section: 2.1 Design and preparation of the multicomponent diffusion-multiple
evidence.quote: the diffusion couple alloys were melted from the appropriate amounts of high purity metals in accordance to the compositions shown in Table 1 via arc melting under an Ar atmosphere. The alloys were inverted and re-melted more than 8 times in order to achieve homogeneous mixing.

evidence.section: 2.1 Design and preparation of the multicomponent diffusion-multiple
evidence.quote: a two-stage heat treatment process of 1240 °C/50h with air cooling and 850 °C/1000h with water cooling was performed. As introduced by Cao et al. [35, 36], 1240 °C/50h was mainly used to form a composition gradient along the couple interfaces quickly at high temperature and 850 °C/1000h was used to achieve phase equilibrium at a target service temperature.

evidence.section: 2.1 Design and preparation of the multicomponent diffusion-multiple
evidence.quote: Hot isostatic pressing (HIP) at 1200 °C/160MPa for 5 h was used to compact the diffusion interfaces and achieve tight interfacial contacts.

evidence.section: 2.2 Compositional measurement and microstructure characterization of the multicomponent diffusion-multiple
evidence.quote: For the γ/γ’ two-phase region in the diffusion couple, the EPMA beam spot was set to a circular diameter of 5 μm to determine the average composition of the local area

evidence.section: 3.1 Microstructure of the diffusion couple alloys after long-term aging
evidence.quote: The base alloy remained as a γ/γ’ two-phase microstructure with a small and cuboidal morphology of γ’ precipitates after aging at 850 °C for 1000 h, indicating that the base alloy had a good microstructural stability.

evidence.section: 3.1 Microstructure of the diffusion couple alloys after long-term aging
evidence.quote: The needle-like secondary phase in alloy + 3Mo was mainly enriched in W, Mo and Ta, and was identified from the selected area diffraction pattern (SADP) as the deleterious μ phase.

machine_learning_models.name: Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT)
machine_learning_models.task: classification of phase equilibrium (γ+γ' two-phase or not)
machine_learning_models.dataset: 1053 compositions and their corresponding phase equilibrium from the multicomponent diffusion-multiple

evidence.section: 2.3 Machine learning
evidence.quote: For the classification model of the phase equilibrium, Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT), Random Forest (RF), K Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Logistic Regression (LR) and Deep Neural Network (DNN) were selected.

machine_learning_models.name: Support Vector Regression (SVR)
machine_learning_models.task: regression of γ' volume fraction, γ' size, γ' roundness
machine_learning_models.target: γ' volume fraction, γ' size, γ' roundness
machine_learning_models.dataset: 1053 compositions and their corresponding microstructural parameters from the multicomponent diffusion-multiple

evidence.section: 2.3 Machine learning
evidence.quote: For the regression models of the γ′ volume fraction, γ′ size, γ′ roundness and γ’ solvus temperature, GBDT, RF, linear regression model (Lin), DNN and support vector regression (SVR) with a radial basis function kernel were selected.

evidence.section: 3.1 Microstructure of the diffusion couple alloys after long-term aging
evidence.quote: The base alloy remained as a γ/γ’ two-phase microstructure with a small and cuboidal morphology of γ’ precipitates after aging at 850 °C for 1000 h, indicating that the base alloy had a good microstructural stability.
